On globber 'error': emits 'error' on the archiver with the fs error. _pending is NOT decremented and the globber has aborted itself (no 'end'), so a pending/later finalize() never completes.
hazard: Do not 'fix' by decrementing _pending on error. [PORTING.md P4: preserved]

behavior: Listeners are attached after construction; the globber begins walking on a setTimeout(0) (deps/readdir-glob/src/index.ts:271), so directory() returns before any fs access and matches arrive after all synchronous append() calls. Returns this.
hazard: Matches may arrive after finalize() was requested; _append has no state check, they are accepted because finalize waits for _pending.

behavior: glob(pattern, options, data): _pending++ first; options = { stat: true, pattern, ...options } (null/undefined options fine; user options can override stat and pattern); walker = new ReaddirGlob(options.cwd || '.', options). `dot` defaults to false here (dotfiles not matched unless requested), unlike directory(). [merged GLOB-FS-098 (node-archiver/lib/core.js:672-673, Archiver.glob (state)): glob() increments _pending immediately and performs NO state check: unlike append/file/directory/symlink it never emits QUEUECLOSED when called after finalize() or abort(), and it does not validate pattern.] [merged GLOB-FS-099 (node-archiver/lib/core.js:674-678, Archiver.glob (options)): Glob options are {stat:true, pattern, ...options}: user options can override both stat (stat:false) and pattern (options.pattern wins over the positional argument). options may be null/undefined (test passes null, test/archiver.js:342).] [merged GLOB-FS-100 (node-archiver/lib/core.js:694, Archiver.glob (cwd)): The globber is `new ReaddirGlob(options.cwd || '.', options)`: cwd defaults to '.', is resolved once at call time, and the full options object (including cwd, ignored by ReaddirGlob) is passed through.]
hazard: glob() has NO QUEUECLOSED / aborted check and no argument validation: calling it after finalize() or abort() still starts a walk and bumps _pending. A port that adds the check for consistency changes behaviour. [merged GLOB-FS-098: Adding the 'missing' QUEUECLOSED check is a behavior change. After finalize the walk still runs; its entries are skipped by _onQueueTask/_onStatQueueTask state checks.] [merged GLOB-FS-099: Do not force stat:true after the spread or let the positional pattern win.] [PORTING.md P6: preserved]

behavior: Per match: globber.pause(); entryData = Object.assign({}, data); entryData.callback = globber.resume.bind(globber); entryData.stats = match.stat; entryData.name = match.relative (relative to cwd); then _append(match.absolute, entryData). User data.prefix/date/mode are honoured; name, stats and callback from user data are overwritten. No data-function support. [merged GLOB-FS-101 (node-archiver/lib/core.js:686-693, Archiver.glob onGlobMatch): Per match: globber.pause(); entryData = shallow copy of data (Object.assign({}, data), data may be undefined); entryData.callback = bound globber.resume; entryData.stats = match.stat; entryData.name = match.relative; then _append(match.absolute, entryData).]
hazard: With user option stat:false, match.stat is undefined so every match goes through the stat queue (lstat). With follow:true stats come from fs.stat, so symlinks are archived as their targets. [merged GLOB-FS-101: name and stats from user data are always overwritten; prefix, date, mode, store etc. are preserved, so data.prefix is how entries get relocated. Each match gets its own copy; the user's object is not mutated.]

behavior: 'end' => _pending--, _maybeFinalize(); 'error' => emit 'error' on archiver (no _pending decrement). Same semantics as directory(). [merged GLOB-FS-104 (node-archiver/lib/core.js:679-682,695-697, Archiver.glob onGlobEnd): On globber 'end': _pending-- and _maybeFinalize() (finalizes if finalize() was requested, no pending globs remain, and both queues are idle).] [merged GLOB-FS-105 (node-archiver/lib/core.js:683-685, Archiver.glob onGlobError): Globber 'error' is re-emitted as archiver 'error' with the same error object; _pending is NOT decremented and nothing else is cleaned up.]
hazard: [merged GLOB-FS-104: Because the last match's task finishes before the globber is resumed, 'end' normally arrives after the queue drained; without this hook the archive would never finalize.] [merged GLOB-FS-105: After a glob error the archive can never auto-finalize (finalize() promise stays pending unless the module errors). Do not 'fix' by decrementing without a deliberate decision.]

behavior: symlink(filepath, target, mode) checks in order, each emitting 'error' and returning this: QUEUECLOSED (finalize requested or aborted); SYMLINKFILEPATHREQUIRED (filepath not a non-empty string, no data); SYMLINKTARGETREQUIRED with data { filepath } (target not a non-empty string); SYMLINKNOTSUPPORTED with data { filepath } (when !_supportsSymlink).

Builds data = { type:'symlink', name: filepath with every '\\' replaced by '/', linkname: target with every '\\' replaced by '/', sourceType:'buffer' } plus mode only if typeof mode === 'number'. The data is NOT passed through _normalizeEntryData: no sanitizePath (leading '/', '../' and drive prefixes are kept; '../file-a' targets preserved), no date, no default mode, no mode masking, no prefix/sourcePath/stats keys.
hazard: Routing symlink() through the normal normalization adds keys, masks mode, strips leading '../' and injects a date, all visible in the JSON oracle and in module output (date undefined lets each module pick its own default).

behavior: _entriesCount++; _queue.push({ data, source: Buffer.concat([]) }) directly on the main queue (no filesystem access at all); returns this.

Exact code => message table: ABORTED 'archive was aborted'; DIRECTORYDIRPATHREQUIRED 'diretory dirpath argument must be a non-empty string value'; DIRECTORYFUNCTIONINVALIDDATA 'invalid data returned by directory custom data function'; ENTRYNAMEREQUIRED 'entry name must be a non-empty string value'; FILEFILEPATHREQUIRED 'file filepath argument must be a non-empty string value'; FINALIZING 'archive already finalizing'; QUEUECLOSED 'queue closed'; NOENDMETHOD 'no suitable finalize/end method defined by module'; DIRECTORYNOTSUPPORTED 'support for directory entries not defined by module'; FORMATSET 'archive format already set'; INPUTSTEAMBUFFERREQUIRED 'input source must be valid Stream or Buffer instance'; MODULESET 'module already set'; SYMLINKNOTSUPPORTED 'support for symlink entries not defined by module'; SYMLINKFILEPATHREQUIRED 'symlink filepath argument must be a non-empty string value'; SYMLINKTARGETREQUIRED 'symlink target argument must be a non-empty string value'; ENTRYNOTSUPPORTED 'entry not supported'. The table itself is not exported.
hazard: Typos are part of the contract: message 'diretory', code INPUTSTEAMBUFFERREQUIRED. FORMATSET and MODULESET are defined but never raised in 8.0.0 (legacy of setFormat/setModule).

behavior: ArchiverError(code, data): Error.captureStackTrace(this, this.constructor); this.message = ERROR_CODES[code] || code (unknown codes use the code string as message); this.code = code; this.data = data (own property, undefined when omitted). Inherits Error via util.inherits, so instanceof Error and instanceof ArchiverError hold; name is inherited 'Error' (the name assignment is commented out).
hazard: An ES `class ArchiverError extends Error` differs observably: message becomes non-enumerable (upstream message/code/data are all own enumerable, so JSON.stringify(err) includes message and code), and the stack header would include the message whereas upstream captures the stack before message is set (stack starts with plain 'Error'). name must stay 'Error', not 'ArchiverError'. [PORTING.md R13: function constructor kept]

target: src/core.ts#Archiver.append ; src/core.ts#Archiver.file ; src/core.ts#Archiver.directory ; src/core.ts#Archiver.symlink ; src/core.ts#Archiver.finalize (emit sites)
behavior: All API-misuse and entry failures are reported by this.emit('error', err) on the still-live stream and the method returns `this`; none of the public methods except finalize (rejected promise) signal failure through their return value, and none throw by design.
hazard: Node semantics: emit('error') without a listener throws the error synchronously from the calling method. readable-stream does not auto-destroy on a manually emitted 'error', so the archive continues to work afterwards; using destroy(err) or throwing breaks continuation tests.

behavior: 'warning' is emitted for non-fatal fs conditions only: lstat failures (raw fs error) and unsupported entry types found on disk (ArchiverError DIRECTORYNOTSUPPORTED / SYMLINKNOTSUPPORTED / ENTRYNOTSUPPORTED with data = entry data). Archiving continues. No listener is required.

_entriesCount is incremented at call time by append(), symlink() and _append() (file/directory/glob matches), decremented only on lstat failure. It is not decremented for unsupported fs entry types, for entries dropped after abort/finalize, or for entries whose module append failed, so entries.total can stay above entries.processed forever.

_fsEntriesTotalBytes grows by stats.size (when truthy) at the moment a filesystem task is resolved (sync for stats-carrying matches, after lstat otherwise), so totals grow while archiving proceeds ('calculated asynchronously and might not be accurate', core.js:849).
hazard: Plain JS number addition; fs.Stats.size is a double. No BigInt.

behavior: `win32 = process.platform === 'win32'` is evaluated once at module load and selects the mode mask (511 vs 4095) and the forced 0755 for stat-derived directory modes. [merged GLOB-FS-052 (node-archiver/lib/core.js:20, win32): `win32 = process.platform === 'win32'` is computed once at module load and selects mode masks in _normalizeEntryData.]
hazard: Mode masking is platform dependent by design; tests branch on win32 too. If mode masking were moved into Rust/WASM the platform flag would have to be injected from JS. [PORTING.md 10.3, TS-10, TS-18: masking stays in TypeScript]

behavior: Because Archiver is a Transform, the full Readable/Writable surface is public: pipe(), on('data'/'end'/'finish'/'close'/'drain'), read(), async iteration, write(), end(), destroy(). Consumers normally call archive.pipe(dest) BEFORE finalize(); doc comment warns end/close/finish may fire right after finalize() (core.js:704-706).
hazard: Replacing the Transform with a plain Readable removes writable-side behaviour that _shutdown() (this.end()) and module.pipe(this) rely on. Backpressure from a slow destination propagates to the module through the 1 MiB highWaterMark buffers on both sides. [PORTING.md R1/V9: node:stream Transform]

behavior: A format module must provide: append(source: Buffer|Readable, data: EntryData, callback(err, entry)) invoked once per entry strictly sequentially; finalize() (or end()) invoked once, synchronously, after the last entry callback; on(event, fn) for at least 'error' and 'end'; pipe(dest) and unpipe(dest). data.sourceType ('buffer'|'stream') tells the module which source kind it got; data.type is 'file'|'directory'|'symlink' with data.linkname for symlinks; data.stats (fs.Stats or false), data.date (Date or undefined for symlink()), data.mode (number or undefined), data.name sanitized (except symlink()). Modules may mutate data; the mutated object is what 'entry' emits.
hazard: The Rust/WASM encoders are sans-IO, so the TS module adapter must reproduce this exact callback/stream contract (callback after the entry's bytes are fully produced, 'end' after finalize output is consumed). [PORTING.md 7.1 ArchiverModule, 7.5]

behavior: `new Archiver()` is constructible but has _module=false and both support flags false: append() of a directory emits DIRECTORYNOTSUPPORTED, symlink() emits SYMLINKNOTSUPPORTED, fs directories/symlinks produce warnings; finalize() emits NOENDMETHOD then the promise executor throws TypeError (false.on is not a function) which rejects the returned promise.

Multiple directory()/glob() walkers run concurrently, each contributing one in-flight match at a time to the single main queue, so their entries interleave in the archive; finalize waits for all (_pending counts active walkers).

file(path, { stats }) with a real fs.Stats skips lstat entirely and uses the given stats for type detection, mode, mtime and byte totals (documented EntryData.stats, core.js:832-833). Such entries are queued synchronously at call time (ordering like append()).

archiver 7.0.0 (the version archiver-zip-encrypted 2.0.0 tests run against) exports a callable: archiver(format, options) === archiver.create(format, options). create throws Error('create(' + format + '): format not registered') for unknown formats, else builds new Archiver(format, options), calls instance.setFormat(format) and instance.setModule(new formats[format](options)).
hazard: The encrypted test suites call archiver.registerFormat('zip-encrypted', ...) and archiver.create/archiver('zip-encrypted', {...}); this API must be provided by the TS layer even though node-archiver 8.0.0 removed it. Zero-skip test reuse depends on it.

behavior: registerFormat(format, module): throws Error('register(' + format + '): format already registered') if the name exists; Error('register(' + format + '): format module invalid') if module is not a function; Error('register(' + format + '): format module missing methods') unless module.prototype.append and module.prototype.finalize are functions; otherwise stores the constructor in a process-wide registry. These are thrown plain Errors, not ArchiverError and not emitted. zip, tar and json are pre-registered (index.js:80-82). [merged ENCRYPTED-002 (archiver-zip-encrypted/test/zip-encrypted.js:10, archiver.registerFormat): Registration is done by the caller, not by the plugin: registerFormat(name, ctor) requires a function whose prototype has append and finalize (inherited from Zip); registering the same name twice throws 'register(zip-encrypted): format already registered' (tests wrap it in try/catch). create(name, options) then does new ctor(options) and pipes it as the module.]
hazard: Registry is module-global: the encrypted tests guard with try/catch or run registerFormat once per file; double registration must throw exactly this way. [merged ENCRYPTED-002: Pinned archiver 8.0.0 (node-archiver/index.js:1-39) has no registerFormat/create at all; the oracle tests need the archiver 7 vending API (registerFormat, create, isRegisteredFormat, duplicate-registration throw) to exist in archiver-wasm.]

behavior: isRegisteredFormat(format) returns true iff a module is registered under that name, else false.

v7 setFormat(format): emits 'error' FORMATSET if _format already set, else stores it. v7 setModule(module): emits 'error' ABORTED if aborted, 'error' MODULESET if _state.module is truthy, else sets _module and calls _modulePipe(). v7 feature detection is via module.supports.directory / module.supports.symlink (_moduleSupports, core.js:260-266) instead of the 8.0.0 _supportsDirectory/_supportsSymlink flags. v7 constructor also accepts (format, options) and defaults format to 'zip' when the first argument is not a string (core.js:30-33).
hazard: 8.0.0 hardcodes support flags in subclasses; a registerFormat-created instance needs the v7 `supports` lookup or the encrypted plugin's directory/symlink entries are rejected. [PORTING.md R19; P23: MODULESET is never raised]

behavior: Directory listing uses callback fs.readdir(dir, {withFileTypes:true}) wrapped in a Promise; entries are fs.Dirent objects with string names (default utf8 encoding, never Buffers).
hazard: Using fs.readdirSync, opendir, or readdir without withFileTypes changes ordering/async timing and loses the Dirent type info used when stat is off.

behavior: ENOTDIR from readdir: rejects with the raw fs error when strict=true, resolves [] when strict=false.
hazard: strict is only true for the root (see GLOB-FS-011); collapsing to always-reject or always-swallow changes directory('some/file') behavior.

behavior: readdir errors with code ENOTSUP, ENOENT, ENAMETOOLONG or 'UNKNOWN' resolve to an empty list (silently ignored), for the root as well as sub-directories.
hazard: A missing root directory therefore yields zero matches and a normal 'end', never an error or warning: archive.directory('does/not/exist') silently adds nothing. Do not add an existence check.

behavior: ELOOP and every other readdir error code (EACCES, EPERM, EMFILE, EIO, ...) reject with the original NodeJS.ErrnoException (unwrapped, same object).
hazard: One unreadable sub-directory anywhere under the root is fatal for the whole walk (see GLOB-FS-040).

behavior: getStat picks fs.stat when followSymlinks is true, fs.lstat otherwise (callback API, non-bigint Stats).
With follow=true, an ENOENT from fs.stat (broken symlink) retries with fs.lstat, so broken links are reported with lstat Stats (isSymbolicLink() true) instead of failing.
hazard: Only ENOENT triggers the fallback; ELOOP/EACCES do not.

behavior: getStat never rejects: any stat/lstat error (other than the follow+ENOENT retry) resolves null.

stat is only fetched when useStat || followSymlinks; a null result falls back to the Dirent (`getStat(...) ?? stat`). So with stat:true a failed stat yields a match whose `stat` is an fs.Dirent, not an fs.Stats.
hazard: Downstream archiver tests `data.stats instanceof Stats` (core.js:98); a Dirent fails that and routes to the lstat queue. Typing match.stat as fs.Stats only is wrong: it is Dirent | Stats.

behavior: Path construction is pure string concatenation: filename = dir + '/' + name; relative = filename.slice(1); absolute = path + '/' + relative, where path = path.resolve(cwd||'.'). Separator is always '/', on every platform.
hazard: Using path.join changes Windows output (absolute becomes 'C:\\root/sub/file' upstream, mixed separators) and collapses the double slash when root is '/' (upstream absolute is '//name'). relative never has a leading './' or backslashes.

behavior: Traversal is sequential depth-first pre-order: entries are visited in exactly the order fs.readdir returned them (no sorting by readdir-glob); a directory is yielded first, then its whole subtree is yielded before the next sibling. One fs operation in flight at a time (await readdir, await getStat per entry).
hazard: Sorting, breadth-first walking, or parallel stat (Promise.all) changes entry order in the produced archive. Order is OS/libuv dependent; do not normalize.

behavior: The root is walked with dir='' and strict=true; every recursive call passes strict=false. Hence root-not-a-directory => ENOTDIR error event, while a sub-entry that claims isDirectory() but fails readdir with ENOTDIR is treated as empty.
The root directory itself is never yielded as a match; only its descendants are.
For a directory entry, shouldSkip(relative) is evaluated (relative WITHOUT trailing slash); if it matches, the directory is neither yielded nor explored; otherwise it is yielded and then recursed.
hazard: skip is tested against 'a/b', whereas pattern/ignore are tested against 'a/b/' (GLOB-FS-031). A skip pattern written with a trailing slash behaves differently from an ignore pattern.

behavior: Non-directory entries (files, symlinks, sockets, FIFOs, devices) are always yielded; skip matchers are never applied to them.
Without follow, isDirectory() comes from the Dirent or lstat, so a symlink to a directory is NOT a directory: it is yielded as a plain match and not descended.
hazard: This is why archiver's directory() retains directory symlinks as symlink entries (test/archiver.js:263-266).

behavior: With follow=true, fs.stat resolves symlinks, so symlinked directories are yielded as directories and descended into. There is no visited-set / cycle detection.
hazard: Cycles terminate only via OS errors: stat ELOOP => null => Dirent fallback (yielded as non-directory); readdir ENAMETOOLONG => []; readdir ELOOP => fatal error. Adding inode tracking changes observable output.

behavior: follow=true forces a stat call on every entry even when options.stat is false, but the emitted payload still omits `stat` unless options.stat is true (see GLOB-FS-037).

Options are normalized into a NEW object: dot, noglobstar, matchBase, nocase, follow, stat, nodir, mark, silent, absolute are coerced with `!!` (default false); pattern, ignore, skip are copied through unchanged (may be undefined). Unknown keys (e.g. cwd) are dropped. `this.options` is this normalized object, not the caller's.
hazard: Truthy non-booleans (1, 'false') become true. `cwd` inside options is ignored by ReaddirGlob; the root is the first constructor argument.

behavior: Signature (cwd?, options?, cb?) with overload: if the second argument is a function it is taken as cb and options becomes {}. options null/undefined => {}.

pattern: if truthy, a string is wrapped to a 1-element array, an array is used as-is; each becomes `new Minimatch(p, {dot, noglobstar, matchBase, nocase})`. Falsy pattern (undefined, null, '') or an empty array => zero matchers, which means 'match everything'.
hazard: Only these four options are forwarded to minimatch for include patterns. Empty string pattern matches everything rather than nothing.

behavior: ignore: string or array, each compiled as `new Minimatch(p, {dot:true})` only: nocase, matchBase and noglobstar are NOT applied to ignore patterns.
hazard: Reusing the include-pattern minimatch options for ignore changes matching (e.g. nocase).

behavior: skip: string or array, each compiled as `new Minimatch(p, {dot:true})`; same restriction as ignore.

Root is `path.resolve(cwd || '.')`, resolved against process.cwd() synchronously at construction time; '' and undefined both mean '.'. The async generator is created eagerly but performs no fs work until the first next().
hazard: A later process.chdir() does not affect an already constructed globber (contrast with file(), GLOB-FS-097).

behavior: Initial public state: paused=false, aborted=false; private inactive=false.

The walk starts via `setTimeout(() => this._next())` with no delay argument (timers phase, >=1ms), so listeners attached synchronously after construction never miss events, and a pause() before the timer fires just marks the walker inactive.
hazard: Starting in a microtask/nextTick/setImmediate changes interleaving against archiver's async.queue (which schedules with queueMicrotask) and against other globbers; keep setTimeout.

behavior: If cb is given, matches are accumulated as strings (match.absolute when options.absolute, else match.relative); 'error' => cb(err); 'end' => cb(null, matches).
hazard: `absolute` affects ONLY this callback result. Event payloads always carry both relative and absolute; archiver never uses cb mode, so glob({absolute:true}) has no effect on entry names. [PORTING.md 7.4, V21: the callback form is not ported, nothing in the package calls it]

behavior: Returns true when any skip matcher matches the directory's relative path (no trailing slash appended).

A candidate matches when (no include matchers OR some include matcher matches) AND no ignore matcher matches AND NOT (nodir && isDirectory). [merged ARCHIVER-CORE-093 (deps/readdir-glob/src/index.ts:278-303, ReaddirGlob match semantics used by glob()): A path matches if (no patterns or any Minimatch pattern matches relative, with '/' appended for directories) and no ignore pattern matches and not (nodir and directory). Emitted match is { relative, absolute, stat } when options.stat else { relative, absolute }; `mark` appends '/' to both for directories. Minimatch options passed: dot, noglobstar, matchBase, nocase; ignore/skip matchers always use dot:true.]
hazard: Evaluation order with short-circuit: include, then ignore, then nodir. [merged ARCHIVER-CORE-093: Directories matched by the pattern become directory entries unless nodir. `ignore` does not prune traversal, `skip` does (index.ts:86-90).]

behavior: Multiple patterns are OR-ed: a path needs to match at least one include pattern; at least one ignore pattern excludes it.
With no pattern, everything matches including dotfiles regardless of the `dot` option (dot is only consulted by minimatch include matchers).
hazard: archiver.directory() passes dot:true with no pattern; dot is effectively a no-op there, dotfiles are included because there is no pattern.

behavior: The string tested by include/ignore matchers is `relative + '/'` for directories and `relative` for everything else.
hazard: Patterns such as '**/*' or 'dir/**' must be evaluated against 'sub/' for directories; dropping the trailing slash changes which directories match.

behavior: nodir suppresses emission of directories only; directories are still traversed and their children emitted.
ignore removes matching files/folders from output but does not prune traversal: children of an ignored folder can still be emitted if they themselves are not ignored.
hazard: Only `skip` prunes. Implementing ignore as a prune changes results and performance characteristics.

behavior: The whole tree under the root is always walked; patterns are filters, there is no static-prefix optimization. archive.glob('test/fixtures/test.txt') with default cwd walks all of process.cwd() (node_modules, .git, ...).
hazard: A 'smart' port that only reads the pattern's literal prefix would hide errors upstream surfaces (e.g. EACCES in an unrelated sub-directory becomes a fatal glob error) and change timing/ordering.

behavior: _next pulls exactly one item with iterator.next() when neither paused nor aborted; isDirectory is taken from the yielded stat (Stats or Dirent).
mark:true appends '/' to BOTH relative and absolute of directory matches (after matching, so matching is unaffected).
hazard: Archiver then uses the slash-terminated absolute as the lstat/readlink path and the slash-terminated relative as entry name.

behavior: 'match' is emitted with a fresh object: {relative, absolute, stat} when options.stat is true; {relative, absolute} (no `stat` key at all) otherwise.
hazard: With stat:false the key is absent, not undefined-valued; archiver then stores entryData.stats = undefined.

behavior: Non-matching items emit nothing; in both cases `this._next()` is called synchronously after the (possible) emit to request the following item.
'end' is emitted once, with no arguments, when the generator is exhausted. It is not emitted after an error or after abort().
hazard: README claims end receives all matches; code passes none.

behavior: On rejection: abort() is called first, then 'error' is emitted with the original error object, then if the error has no `code` and options.silent is false it is also printed with console.error(err).
hazard: Order matters: globber.aborted is already true inside error listeners. fs errors (with code) are not printed.

behavior: The .catch also covers exceptions thrown synchronously by 'match' or 'end' listeners (they run inside the .then callback): the walk is aborted, the exception is re-emitted as 'error', and (no code) logged via console.error unless silent. [merged ARCHIVER-CORE-094 (deps/readdir-glob/src/index.ts:285-335, ReaddirGlob pause/resume): pause() sets paused; the next _next() call sees it and marks the walker inactive; resume() clears paused and restarts iteration only if inactive. A synchronous pause+resume inside the 'match' handler therefore just continues. Iterator rejection => abort() + emit 'error' (+ console.error when the error has no code and !silent).]
hazard: In archiver, anything throwing inside onGlobMatch (e.g. readlinkSync failing in _updateQueueTaskWithStats, core.js:467, or emit('error') with no listener) aborts the glob, surfaces as archiver 'error', and 'end' never fires so _pending stays >0. A port using a plain loop + try/catch around fs only would lose this. [merged ARCHIVER-CORE-094: Exceptions thrown inside archiver's match handler (e.g. readlinkSync failure, TypeError from sanitizePath) are caught by this promise chain and surface as globber 'error' => archiver 'error', not as uncaught exceptions.]

behavior: If the 'error' emit itself throws (no listener, or listener throws), the exception escapes the .catch handler and becomes an unhandled promise rejection; the console.error line is skipped.
When _next is entered while paused or aborted it does nothing except set inactive=true.

abort() only sets aborted=true: no event is emitted, the generator is not returned/closed, and an already in-flight iterator.next() still resolves and still emits its 'match' (the check happens only at the next _next()).
hazard: Do not emit 'end' or call generator.return() on abort. Archiver itself never calls globber.abort().

behavior: pause() only sets paused=true; an in-flight item still gets emitted (at most one 'match' after pause), after which the walker parks with inactive=true.

resume() clears paused and restarts the pull loop only if inactive is true (then sets inactive=false and calls _next synchronously). Calling resume while a pull is in flight, or synchronously inside a 'match' listener, does not start a second concurrent pull.
hazard: A naive resume() that always calls _next() double-drives the iterator and duplicates/reorders matches (archiver's directory() calls resume synchronously in the listener for ignored matches, core.js:626-629).

behavior: resume() after abort(): paused=false, _next runs and immediately re-parks (inactive=true); nothing is ever emitted again.

Default export is a factory `(root?, options?, cb?) => new ReaddirGlob(...)` with the class attached as readdirGlob.ReaddirGlob; the first parameter is the root directory despite being named `pattern` in the source.
hazard: archiver uses both forms: `const { ReaddirGlob } = readdirGlob` (core.js:19) and `readdirGlob(dirpath, opts)` (core.js:632).

behavior: ReaddirGlob is a plain EventEmitter (not a stream) with events match:[Match], end:[], error:[ErrnoException]; public fields options, paused, aborted.

Matching semantics are those of minimatch ^10.2.2 (Minimatch class, .match(path)); upstream install resolves 10.2.5 nested under readdir-glob while a different 9.0.9 sits at top level for other packages.
hazard: Pin minimatch to the ^10.2.2 line for the port; do not reimplement glob matching in Rust (fixed decision: minimatch stays an npm dependency). [PORTING.md 12.2]

target: src/core.ts#(module imports: createReadStream, lstat, readlinkSync, Stats from node:fs)
behavior: core.js touches fs through exactly four bindings: createReadStream (459), lstat (392), readlinkSync (467) and Stats (98, instanceof). No stat, readdir, open or access calls exist in core.js.
hazard: Do not introduce fs.stat (would follow symlinks) or async readlink (changes ordering/exception path).

behavior: When _updateQueueTaskWithStats returns null (unsupported entry type) on the synchronous path, nothing is queued and data.callback is never invoked; _entriesCount stays incremented.
hazard: For glob()/directory() this leaves the globber paused forever (a FIFO/socket/device inside a globbed tree stalls the walk: 'end' never fires, _pending never reaches 0, finalize never completes). Upstream behavior; the port must decide consciously, tests do not cover it.

behavior: With statConcurrency > 1, file() entries enter _queue in lstat completion order, not call order; append()/symlink() entries bypass the stat queue and can overtake earlier file() calls.
hazard: Archive entry order for file() is nondeterministic upstream; a port must not serialize differently in a way tests could observe (keep the two-queue structure, do not await lstat inline in file()).

behavior: readlinkSync exceptions are not caught. Three paths: (a) file(path, { stats }) with a real fs.Stats runs _updateQueueTaskWithStats synchronously inside _append (core.js:97-99), so the exception is thrown out of file() itself, after _entriesCount was incremented; (b) on the stat-queue path it is thrown out of the lstat callback (uncaught exception); (c) on the glob path it is caught by readdir-glob's promise chain and becomes a glob 'error' (GLOB-FS-041).
hazard: Converting to async readlink with a rejected promise changes both failure modes. [PORTING.md 13.3: all three paths preserved; differential case D8]

behavior: Branch order is isFile, then isDirectory, then isSymbolicLink. With fs.stat-derived Stats (glob follow:true) a symlink to a file is isFile() and is archived as regular file content (createReadStream follows the link).
Without data.name the entry name is the given filepath after sanitizePath (e.g. 'test/fixtures/test.txt' stays, '/abs/x' => 'abs/x', '../x' => 'x') (test/archiver.js:307-309).
file() on a directory path produces a single directory entry (no recursion); file() on a symlink produces a symlink entry, because the type is decided from lstat.

lazystream.Readable(fn, options) is a PassThrough (readable-stream 2.3.8, default 16KiB highWaterMark, non-object mode) whose instance-level _read is patched; the constructor emits a synthetic 'readable' event immediately (no listeners yet, so a no-op). Archiver passes no options.
hazard: It is a different readable-stream major (v2) than core.js uses (v4); the port can use node:stream PassThrough but must keep the 'open on first read' contract. [PORTING.md R1/V9, 7.4: node:stream PassThrough constructed with autoDestroy: false and emitClose: false, because readable-stream 2.3.8 never destroys the stream after its end and never emits 'close'; the default highWaterMark is 64 KiB on Node 22 and later (16 KiB upstream and on Node 18 and 20)] [PORTING.md 7.4, V21: the options parameter is not ported, archiver passes none]

behavior: On the first _read call only: the instance override is deleted, fn is invoked (createReadStream opens the fd), source 'error' is forwarded as 'error' on the lazy stream, source.pipe(lazy) is set up, and then the prototype _read runs with the same arguments.
hazard: The factory runs exactly once and only when a consumer starts reading; data handlers/pipe must be attached by the module before any file descriptor exists. [PORTING.md 7.4, TS-41: beforeFirstCall keeps its method parameter and the computed delete instance[method]; V9: a factory that throws becomes an 'error' event instead of an exception out of read(), unreachable from archiver]

behavior: Because _queue has concurrency 1 and the read stream is created on first read, at most one file descriptor from file()/glob()/directory() entries is open at a time regardless of how many entries are queued or of statConcurrency.
hazard: Eagerly creating read streams (or fs.open) at stat time reintroduces EMFILE on large trees; reading whole files into memory changes memory profile.

behavior: Open/read failures (file deleted or made unreadable between lstat and read, EISDIR, ...) surface as an 'error' event on the lazy stream at consumption time, not at file()/stat time; the lazy stream is not ended or destroyed by the error (pipe does not propagate).
hazard: Handling depends on the format plugin: zip listens with source.once('error') (deps/compress-commons/lib/archivers/zip/zip-archive-output-stream.js:104), json/tar-without-stats use collectStream's error callback (utils.js:9), but tar with stats just does source.pipe(entry) with no error listener (node-archiver/lib/plugins/tar.js:64-69), so the error is an unhandled 'error' event. Preserve or consciously document any change. [PORTING.md P22: preserved] [PORTING.md V9, 7.4: 'not ended or destroyed by the error' holds with and without an 'error' listener because the lazy PassThrough has autoDestroy: false; with the node:stream default the no-listener path would destroy it]

behavior: The fs path sets data.sourceType='stream' plus data.stats for files, which makes the tar plugin stream the file with size = stats.size taken at stat time; stream sources without stats (append(stream)) are fully buffered via collectStream first.
hazard: File size is trusted from the earlier lstat; a file that changes size between stat and read produces a tar size-mismatch error. The Rust tar encoder must take the declared size up front for the streaming path. [PORTING.md 6.12, 7.8: the Rust Pack has no entry state; size check and body bytes are the TypeScript Sink]

behavior: file() paths are passed verbatim to lstat and later to createReadStream, so relative paths resolve against process.cwd() at the time each fs call runs (not at file() call time). glob()/directory() entries use the pre-resolved absolute path from the match.
hazard: Eagerly path.resolve()-ing in file() changes data.sourcePath (observable in 'entry' events and JSON output) and chdir behavior.

behavior: Entry name is the path relative to cwd with '/' separators (e.g. glob('**/*', {cwd:'test/fixtures/directory/subdir/'}) yields 'level1.txt', 'subsub/level2.txt'; with default cwd the name includes the full relative path 'test/fixtures/test.txt') (test/archiver.js:341-360). The source file is read from match.absolute.

The walk is strictly one-match-at-a-time: the globber is paused on every match and resumed only when that entry's queue task has completed (after the module wrote the entry), so no further readdir/stat happens while an entry is being archived.
hazard: Collecting all matches first, or not pausing, changes memory use, interleaving with other sources, and the abort/finalize race behavior.

behavior: If the caller sets stat:false, match.stat is absent, entryData.stats is undefined, and every match goes through the lstat stat queue (still resumed via data.callback on success).
hazard: Combined with follow:true this yields lstat-typed entries (symlink entries for followed directory links plus their children).

behavior: ignore, skip, dot, follow, mark, nodir, nocase, matchBase, noglobstar, silent are forwarded untouched to ReaddirGlob; `absolute` is forwarded but has no effect on entries. Default dot is false for glob() (dotfiles excluded unless the pattern names them).
hazard: glob() and directory() differ: directory() includes dotfiles and directories, glob('**/*') excludes dotfiles and includes directories unless nodir.

behavior: With mark:true directory matches reach _append with a trailing '/' on both name and filepath; lstat/readlink are called on the slash-terminated absolute path.

The object returned by the data function replaces entryData wholesale. Returning null passes the typeof check and reaches _append(match.absolute, null), which substitutes {} (name becomes the absolute path, stats lost, lstat queue used, no callback). Returning a new object without `callback` likewise never resumes the globber.
hazard: The resume hook lives on the data object itself; a port that keeps the resume callback in a closure instead would silently 'fix' these stalls and change behavior.

behavior: Final name = sanitizePath(destpath + '/' + match.relative) when destpath is non-empty, else sanitizePath(match.relative); directory entries get a trailing slash (e.g. 'directory/subdir/', 'Win/DS/level0.txt', 'test/fixtures/directory/subdir/subsublink' for a directory symlink).
A non-existent dirpath silently produces no entries and a normal end; a dirpath that is a regular file produces an ENOTDIR 'error' on the archiver (strict root).

Each glob()/directory() call owns an independent globber started on its own 0ms timer; all feed the single concurrency-1 _queue, so entries of several walks interleave in arrival order (one match per globber can be queued at a time).
hazard: Running walks sequentially (one after the other) changes archive entry order relative to upstream.

behavior: Directory and symlink entries carry `Buffer.concat([])` (a zero-length Buffer) as source with sourceType 'buffer'; the symlink target travels only in data.linkname.

The object emitted with 'entry' is the normalized data object itself, including fs-derived fields: sourcePath, sourceType, stats (fs.Stats), callback (for glob entries), prefix:null, linkname. 'progress' reports fs.totalBytes/processedBytes as sums of stats.size for entries that have stats (directories and symlinks included when size is truthy).
hazard: The JSON format plugin stringifies this object (node-archiver/lib/plugins/json.js:40,61), so stats/sourcePath/sourceType appear in JSON archives; stripping internal fields changes output. totalBytes grows asynchronously as stats arrive.

behavior: Plugin options = shallow spread of user options over defaults {comment:"", forceUTC:false, namePrependSlash:false, store:false}; result stored as this.options and passed to new ZipStream(options). options may be undefined (spread of undefined is fine).
hazard: forceUTC is a vestigial key never read anywhere; the real switch is forceLocalTime (default falsy). Do not wire forceUTC to anything. Keys explicitly set to undefined by the user override the defaults (spread semantics).

behavior: The spread is shallow: options.zlib is the user's own object and is later mutated in place by ZipStream/_defaults (zlib.level gets written). The copied top-level object is also mutated (zlib, level deleted, store, namePrependSlash, forceZip64, forceLocalTime).
hazard: A port that deep-clones or freezes options changes observable mutation of the caller's zlib object; low priority but mechanical port should keep in-place mutation. [PORTING.md TS-08: in-place mutation kept]

behavior: append(source, data, callback) forwards unchanged to engine.entry(source, data, callback); return value discarded (void).
finalize() calls engine.finalize(); plugin has no end() method, so core's _moduleFinalize takes the finalize branch.

on(), pipe(), unpipe() apply all arguments to the engine's stream methods and return the engine's return value (engine for on, destination for pipe, engine for unpipe). Core calls module.on('error'), module.pipe(archiver), module.on('end').
hazard: The plugin object itself is not an EventEmitter; only these three methods exist. A TS port must still give the core an object with on/pipe/unpipe semantics of a Node stream.

behavior: options = options || {}; options.zlib = options.zlib || {} (any falsy zlib replaced by a fresh object).

If typeof options.level === 'number' && options.level >= 0 then options.zlib.level = options.level (overwriting any zlib.level) and delete options.level. Negative or non-number level is left in place and ignored.
hazard: level:-1 at top level is NOT forwarded (so default level 1 applies), while zlib:{level:-1} IS honoured (zlib default 6). NaN fails >= 0 and is ignored.

behavior: If !options.forceZip64 and options.zlib.level is the number 0, options.store = true (archive-wide default method becomes STORED). With forceZip64 truthy and level 0, store is not forced: entries are method 8 deflated at zlib level 0.
hazard: Easy to drop the forceZip64 exception. It changes method field (0 vs 8), descriptor flag and version needed for buffer sources.

behavior: options.namePrependSlash = options.namePrependSlash || false.
After super(options): if options.comment is truthy and options.comment.length > 0, this.setComment(options.comment). Otherwise archive comment stays "".

Entry data = spread of caller data over defaults {type:'file', name:null, namePrependSlash:this.options.namePrependSlash, linkname:null, date:null, mode:null, store:this.options.store, comment:''}. Unknown keys (prefix, stats, sourcePath, sourceType...) pass through untouched and are ignored.
hazard: Own keys with value undefined override defaults: {store: undefined} disables an archive-wide store:true; {comment: undefined} later throws TypeError at data.comment.length (index.js:134), thrown synchronously, not via callback.

behavior: Only if data.name is truthy: data.name = sanitizePath(data.name). Then if type is not symlink and the sanitized name ends with '/', type is forced to 'directory' (even if caller said 'file'); else if type was 'directory', '/' is appended.
hazard: A symlink whose name ends in '/' stays type symlink here but ZipArchiveEntry.isDirectory() is name based and will treat it as a directory for mode bits (see ZIP-071).

behavior: Directories and symlinks always get data.store = true regardless of options or per-entry store.
data.date = dateify(data.date) always, so date is always a Date instance (possibly Invalid Date) before reaching ZipArchiveEntry.setTime.

Falsy input (null, undefined, 0, '') => new Date() (now). Date instance => same object. string => new Date(string) (may be Invalid Date, local-time parsing rules of JS Date for non-ISO strings). Anything else (numbers, objects) => new Date() (now).
hazard: A numeric epoch timestamp is NOT honoured; it becomes now. A port that helpfully accepts numbers changes bytes. Invalid date strings are not rejected (see ZIP-086).

behavior: sanitizePath(p) = normalizePath(p, false) then remove one leading match of /^\w+:/ (ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_]+ followed by ':', e.g. 'C:' or 'http:'), then remove one leading run matching /^(\.\.\/|\/)+/ (any mix of '../' and '/' repeated).
hazard: Not idempotent: 'c:c:/x' => 'c:/x' => 'x' on a second pass. './' is not stripped, inner '..' segments are not resolved, a bare '..' or trailing '/..' is kept. \w is ASCII only (no unicode flag). Rust regex \w is Unicode by default; use (?-u) or hand code. [PORTING.md R6: one copy per layer; applied at the same three call sites as upstream]

behavior: Throws TypeError('expected path to be a string') for non strings. Returns '/' for input exactly '/' or a single backslash. Returns input unchanged when length <= 1. Otherwise splits on runs of '/' or backslash (/[/\\]+/) and joins with '/', so backslashes become '/', repeated separators collapse, and (stripTrailing === false) a trailing separator is preserved as a single trailing '/'.
hazard: length is UTF-16 code units. Leading separator is preserved by split/join (empty first segment) and only removed by the later regex in sanitizePath. [PORTING.md R6: one copy per layer] [PORTING.md 6.6: with strip_trailing = true (stripTrailing !== false) the trailing empty segment is popped, index.js:31-33; no upstream call site passes true, the branch is ported and tested all the same] [PORTING.md 7.4, V21: the TypeScript copy has no stripTrailing parameter; the Rust copy keeps both values]

behavior: If length > 4, path[3] is a backslash, path[2] is '?' or '.', and the first two chars are two backslashes, the first two chars are dropped and prefix '//' is prepended to the joined result (e.g. backslash-backslash-?-backslash-C:-backslash-foo => '//?/C:/foo'); sanitizePath then strips the leading slashes giving '?/C:/foo'.
hazard: Obscure branch; a hand written normaliser will miss it. The drive strip regex does not fire because the string no longer starts with a word char. [PORTING.md R6: one copy per layer]

behavior: If callback is not a function it is replaced by this._emitErrorCallback bound to the stream, which emits 'error' on the engine only when err is truthy.

After normalisation, if data.type is not 'file', 'directory' or 'symlink': callback(new Error(data.type + ' entries not currently supported')) and return undefined. Nothing is written, processing flag untouched.
hazard: Reported through the callback, never thrown. Message is the plain concatenation, e.g. 'undefined entries not currently supported'.

behavior: If typeof data.name !== 'string' or its length is 0 after sanitising: callback(new Error('entry name must be a non-empty string value')), return undefined. Names that sanitise to '' (e.g. '/', '../', 'C:') hit this.
hazard: A truthy non-string name (number, object) never reaches this check: sanitizePath throws TypeError('expected path to be a string') synchronously first.

behavior: If type is 'symlink' and typeof data.linkname !== 'string': callback(new Error('entry linkname must be a non-empty string value when type equals symlink')), return undefined. An empty string linkname passes despite the message.
hazard: Do not add an emptiness check; '' is accepted and yields an empty stored entry.

behavior: Order of mutations on a fresh ZipArchiveEntry: new ZipArchiveEntry(data.name) (name sanitised again, UTF-8 flag evaluated); setTime(data.date, options.forceLocalTime); if data.namePrependSlash then setName(data.name, true); if data.store then setMethod(0); if data.comment.length > 0 then setComment; symlink default mode; setUnixMode if mode numeric; symlink source replacement; super.entry.
hazard: Order matters: setUnixMode consults isDirectory() of the final (possibly slash prefixed) name; the UTF-8 flag is sticky across the two setName calls.

behavior: When data.namePrependSlash is truthy (per-entry value, defaulting to the archive option) the entry name becomes '/' + sanitise(data.name). The prefix is added after sanitising so it survives; e.g. 'a/b.txt' is stored as '/a/b.txt' in both LFH and CFH.
hazard: Per-entry data.namePrependSlash overrides the archive option in both directions.

behavior: data.store truthy => entry.setMethod(0) (STORED). Otherwise method stays -1 and is resolved to DEFLATED (8) in _normalizeEntry.
Per-entry comment is set only when data.comment.length > 0; default ''. The comment appears only in the central file header.
hazard: Non-string comment with a length (Buffer, array) is accepted by JS; restrict to string in TS types but do not coerce. [PORTING.md 5.6, V14: no coercion; a non-string comment that passes the length test is rejected by wasmString with a TypeError before the wasm call]

behavior: For symlinks with a non-number mode, data.mode = 40960 (0o120000). For symlinks with a numeric mode, data.mode |= 40960. Result for archiver.symlink() without mode: external attributes 0xA0000020 (2684354592), as asserted by node-archiver/test/plugins.js:227.
hazard: data.mode is mutated on the caller's (spread copy) object. Permission bits are zero when no mode was given: do not default to 0777.

behavior: setUnixMode(data.mode) is called only when typeof data.mode === 'number'. Otherwise the entry keeps platform FAT (0), external attributes 0 and version-made-by 0x002D. Via archiver core, files and directories always arrive with a numeric mode (core.js:285-302) so they are always platform UNIX (3); only direct engine use hits the FAT path.
hazard: mode:null/undefined must leave platform byte 0 and exattr 0, not apply 0644/0755 defaults in this layer.

behavior: For symlinks the source argument is discarded and replaced by Buffer.from(data.linkname) (UTF-8). The entry is therefore a STORED buffer entry whose content is the link target; sizes and CRC are in the LFH, no data descriptor, version needed 10.
Returns super.entry(...) which is `this` on the accepted path and undefined on every error path.
finalize() simply calls this.finish().

If typeof o !== 'object' o = {}; if typeof o.zlib !== 'object' o.zlib = {}; if typeof o.zlib.level !== 'number' o.zlib.level = 1 (ZLIB_BEST_SPEED); o.forceZip64 = !!o.forceZip64; o.forceLocalTime = !!o.forceLocalTime. Returns the same (mutated) object.
hazard: Default deflate level is 1, not zlib's 6. Compressed sizes in headers depend on it. null passes the typeof object test and would throw; unreachable via ZipStream.

behavior: The whole options object is passed to the Transform constructor (so user supplied highWaterMark, objectMode etc. take effect on the engine stream); this.options = same object; _entry = null; _entries = []; _archive = {centralLength:0, centralOffset:0, comment:'', finish:false, finished:false, processing:false, forceZip64, forceLocalTime}; offset = 0 (from base).
hazard: Via node-archiver/index.js:12 the raw user options (not Archiver's merged defaults) reach the plugin, so the engine stream uses Node's default highWaterMark unless the user set one.

behavior: Transform is an identity pass-through: every chunk written to the engine is emitted unchanged on its readable side.

write(chunk, cb) override: if chunk is truthy, this.offset += chunk.length, then super.write(chunk, cb). offset is the running archive position used for LFH offsets, central directory offset/length. getBytesWritten() returns offset.
hazard: For string chunks length is UTF-16 units, not bytes. Strings are only written for ASCII names/comments (equal) and for the archive comment (may be non-ASCII, see ZIP-101). Rust must track u64 byte offset; JS number is exact to 2^53. [PORTING.md 7.5, ZIP-135: the TypeScript offset is the one offset and is handed to Rust with setOffset; V5 for the comment]

behavior: source = source || null, so undefined, '', 0, false become null; then normalizeInputSource: null => Buffer.alloc(0); string => Buffer.from(string) UTF-8; a stream without _readableState (old style) is piped into a new PassThrough which is used instead; everything else unchanged.
If ae is not instanceof ArchiveEntry: callback(new Error('not a valid instance of ArchiveEntry')), return undefined.
If _archive.finish or _archive.finished is set: callback(new Error('unacceptable entry after finish')), return undefined.

If _archive.processing is true: callback(new Error('already processing an entry')), return undefined. Only one entry at a time; no internal queue (archiver core's queue with concurrency 1 serialises).
hazard: The sans-IO Rust encoder needs the same single-open-entry state and the same error text if the TS layer surfaces it. [PORTING.md 6.8, 7.5: guards in both layers, the TypeScript flags are authoritative]

behavior: Sets processing = true, calls _normalizeEntry(ae), sets this._entry = ae, coerces source, then Buffer => _appendBuffer, stream (is-stream) => _appendStream, else processing = false and callback(new Error('input source must be valid Stream or Buffer instance')). Returns this on buffer/stream paths.
hazard: On the invalid-source path _normalizeEntry has already mutated the entry and _entry stays set; nothing has been written.

behavior: finish(): if an entry is processing, only sets _archive.finish = true (central directory is written later from _afterAppend); otherwise calls _finish() immediately.
hazard: There is no guard against calling finish twice when idle: a second call would write a second central directory and call end() again. Archiver core guards this.

behavior: If entry method is -1 (unset) it becomes 8 (DEFLATED). If method is 8, the data-descriptor GPB bit is set and version needed becomes 20. This runs before the source type or length is known.
hazard: Deflated entries ALWAYS use a data descriptor, even for in-memory buffers whose size and CRC could be known up front.

behavior: If ae.getTime() === -1 (time never set) the entry time is set to now with the archive forceLocalTime flag. Then ae._offsets = {file:0, data:0, contents:0}.
hazard: Sentinel is the number -1 compared by identity; a DOS time of 0 (from an Invalid Date) is a set value and is NOT replaced. Model as Option<u32>.

behavior: A zero-length buffer forces method STORED (0) regardless of the requested method.
hazard: Quirk: for a default (deflate) entry _normalizeEntry already set the descriptor bit and version 20, and these are NOT undone. An empty non-store file from a buffer is written as: version needed 20, GPB bit 3 set, method 0, CRC/sizes zero in LFH, no data, followed by a 16 byte data descriptor (sig, 0, 0, 0). An empty entry with store:true (and every directory) has version 10, no bit 3, no descriptor. [PORTING.md P14: preserved]

behavior: For method 0 with a buffer source: size = compressedSize = source.length and crc = crc32.buf(source) >>> 0 are set BEFORE the local header is written, so the LFH carries real CRC and sizes (unless descriptor bit already set, see ZIP-044/ZIP-058).
Sequence for stored buffers: LFH, then the whole source buffer as one write, then _afterAppend(ae), then callback(null, ae) synchronously inside entry().
hazard: Callback is synchronous for stored buffers and asynchronous for deflated ones; TS layer must not assume either (core wraps with setImmediate).

behavior: For method 8 with a buffer: LFH written (zeros for CRC/sizes because descriptor bit is set), then the buffer is fed in one end(source) call to the _smartStream pipeline; descriptor follows the compressed data.

Any other method value with a buffer source: the LFH has ALREADY been written, then callback(new Error('compression method ' + method + ' not implemented')). _afterAppend is not called: the entry is not recorded in the central directory and processing stays true forever (later entries fail with 'already processing an entry', finish() only sets the flag).
hazard: Unreachable via ZipStream (methods are only -1/0/8) but reachable by subclasses (encrypted plugin uses method 99 and overrides _appendBuffer). Keep the error string.

behavior: Stream sources always set the data-descriptor bit and version needed 20 (also for STORED), write the LFH with zero CRC/sizes, then pipe source into the _smartStream pipeline.
hazard: Stored stream entries still get bit 3 + descriptor + version 20; stored buffer entries get neither. The Rust API must take 'source kind' (buffer vs stream) as an input, it is not derivable from data. [PORTING.md 6.8: Source::Buffer { len, crc } / Source::Stream]

behavior: On the first 'error' of the source: the error is re-emitted on the smart stream (captured into the closure variable) and smart.end() is called. The pipeline then ends normally: CRC/sizes of the partial data are recorded, the entry IS pushed to the central directory, its data descriptor is written, and the callback receives (err, ae).
hazard: A port that aborts the entry on source error and drops it from the central directory produces different bytes. The partial entry stays in the archive. [PORTING.md P16: preserved]

behavior: Method 8 => new DeflateCRC32Stream(this.options.zlib) (raw deflate, no zlib/gzip wrapper). Any other method => new CRC32Stream() pass-through (data stored verbatim). The processor is piped into the archive stream with {end:false}.
hazard: Raw deflate only: no 2 byte zlib header or adler32 trailer. flate2 must use Compress::new(level, false) / DeflateEncoder, not ZlibEncoder.

behavior: On processor 'end': crc = digest().readUInt32BE(0) (unsigned), size = process.size() (uncompressed byte count), compressedSize = process.size(true); then _afterAppend(ae); then callback(error, ae) where error is the last captured processor error or null.
hazard: For CRC32Stream size(true) ignores its argument and returns rawSize, so csize == size for stored streams.

behavior: The first 'error' on the processor is only stored; nothing is emitted on the archive stream. If the processor errors without ever emitting 'end' (a real zlib failure) the entry callback is never called and processing stays true.
hazard: Decide deliberately in TS whether to preserve the hang; Rust deflate cannot fail in the same way. Document rather than invent a new error. [PORTING.md V8, 13.4: the failing zlib processor does not exist in archiver-wasm; a failure of the wasm engine during an entry is delivered through the entry callback by SmartStream._fail, processing stays true]

behavior: The whole options.zlib object is handed to zlib.DeflateRaw: level (default 1 from _defaults), memLevel, strategy, windowBits, chunkSize, dictionary, flush, finishFlush. Invalid values (e.g. level 10) throw a RangeError from the DeflateRaw constructor synchronously out of entry(), AFTER the local file header has been written.
hazard: miniz_oxide via flate2 only honours level (0-9); memLevel/strategy/windowBits/dictionary cannot be reproduced. Deflate bytes need not match, but level -1 must map to 6, and out-of-range validation should stay in TS to keep the thrown error type. [PORTING.md R15/V2: only level reaches Rust, as resolveLevel(this.options.zlib) (ZIP-136); the bag is validated in TypeScript] [PORTING.md 7.7: validateZlibOptions calls zlib.createDeflateRaw(options).close(), which is new zlib.DeflateRaw(options) at run time]

behavior: Pushes the entry onto _entries (central directory order = completion order = append order), writes the data descriptor iff the entry's descriptor bit is set, sets processing = false and _entry = null, then if finish was requested and not yet finished calls _finish().
hazard: When finalize was requested mid-entry, the central directory, EOCD and end() all happen inside _afterAppend BEFORE the entry callback fires.

behavior: LFH, 30 fixed bytes, all little-endian: signature 0x04034b50 (50 4B 03 04); version needed (2); GPB flags (2); method (2); DOS time+date as one 32-bit value (4); CRC32 (4); compressed size (4); uncompressed size (4); name length (2); extra length (2); then name bytes; then extra bytes.
hazard: Compressed size precedes uncompressed size. Time and date are a single LE u32 (time in low 16 bits).

behavior: If the descriptor bit is set, CRC, compressed size and uncompressed size in the LFH are all written as 4 zero bytes each (12 zero bytes), even when the values are known. Otherwise the real crc/csize/size are written with 32-bit truncation.

If ae.isZip64() at LFH time (only possible for a stored buffer larger than 0xFFFFFFFF bytes, since sizes are otherwise still 0): descriptor bit is forced on and version needed becomes 45. Consequently LFH sizes/CRC are zero and an 8-byte-size data descriptor follows the data.
hazard: No ZIP64 extra field is ever written in a local file header by this code. Do not 'fix' this by adding one. [PORTING.md P15: preserved] [PORTING.md V16, 17.2: reachable from TypeScript because the stored payload is written by TypeScript and never enters wasm; cargo test plain_entry_shapes, slow case S3]

behavior: ae._offsets.file = offset before the signature (used as LFH offset in the CFH); ae._offsets.data = offset right after the DOS time field (file + 14, i.e. position of the CRC field); ae._offsets.contents = offset after name and extra (start of file data).

behavior: If the UTF-8 GPB bit is set, name (and in the CFH the comment) are converted with Buffer.from(str) (UTF-8) and their byte lengths are used. If not set, they are written as JS strings and .length is used; by construction they are pure ASCII then, so bytes are identical to UTF-8.

behavior: Data descriptor for non-zip64 entries, 16 bytes LE: signature 0x08074b50 (50 4B 07 08), CRC32 (4), compressed size (4), uncompressed size (4). The signature is always present.
If ae.isZip64() (size or csize > 0xFFFFFFFF) the descriptor is 24 bytes: signature, CRC32 (4), compressed size (8 LE), uncompressed size (8 LE).
hazard: Chosen by the entry's sizes only; forceZip64 does NOT switch descriptors to 8-byte sizes, and an entry that is zip64 only because of its offset keeps the 16 byte form.

behavior: CFH, 46 fixed bytes LE: signature 0x02014b50 (50 4B 01 02); version made by (2); version needed (2); GPB (2); method (2); DOS time/date (4); CRC32 (4); compressed size (4); uncompressed size (4); name length (2); extra length (2); comment length (2); disk number start = 0 (2); internal attributes (2); external attributes (4); LFH offset (4); then name, extra, comment bytes.
Version made by = (platform << 8) | 45. Platform is 3 (UNIX) once setUnixMode has been called, else 0 (FAT). Bytes on disk: 2D 03 for unix entries, 2D 00 otherwise.
hazard: Always 45 in the low byte, independent of whether zip64 is used.

behavior: Per entry: initial 10; 20 when method is DEFLATED or the source is a stream (descriptor); 45 when the entry is zip64 at LFH time or (in the CFH only) when isZip64() or the LFH offset exceeds 0xFFFFFFFF.
hazard: LFH and CFH of the same entry can disagree: a streamed entry that turns out > 4 GiB has 20 in its LFH and 45 in its CFH. Do not back-patch.

behavior: If ae.isZip64() or ae._offsets.file > 0xFFFFFFFF: the CFH writes 0xFFFFFFFF for compressed size, uncompressed size AND LFH offset (all three, regardless of which overflowed); version needed set to 45; entry extra is REPLACED by a 28 byte ZIP64 extra: header id 0x0001 (2), data size 24 (2), uncompressed size (8), compressed size (8), LFH offset (8).

behavior: Internal file attributes are always 0 in this pipeline (ZipStream never calls setInternalAttributes); disk number start is the constant SHORT_ZERO.

mode |= (isDirectory() ? 0o040000 : 0o100000); external attributes = ((mode << 16) | (isDirectory() ? 0x10 : 0x20)) >>> 0; this.mode = mode & 0xfff; platform = 3. Examples asserted by tests: file 0644 => 0x81A40020 (2175008800); file 0777 => 0x81FF0020 (2180972576); dir 0755 => 0x41ED0010 (1106051088); symlink without perms => 0xA0000020.

In Rust: ((mode as u32) << 16) | dos with wrapping. [PORTING.md 10.3: i32 arithmetic exactly as pinned there, one final `as u32`; not u32 shifts]

behavior: With forceLocalTime falsy (the default) the fields come from the UTC getters (getUTCFullYear ... getUTCSeconds); with forceLocalTime true they come from the local-time getters of the process timezone (TZ env, DST aware).

behavior: If year >= 2044 the result is the constant 2141175677 (0x7F9FBF7D = 2043-12-31 23:59:58).

behavior: ZIP64 EOCD locator, 20 bytes LE, immediately after the record: signature 0x07064b50 (50 4B 06 07); disk holding the ZIP64 EOCD = 0 (4); offset of the ZIP64 EOCD record = centralOffset + centralLength (8); total number of disks = 1 (4).

Record order: 'path' (only if name truthy), 'linkpath' (only if linkname truthy), then every enumerable key of opts.pax. Each record is '<len> <key>=<value>

hazard: Useful for round-trip tests only; not part of the writer.

behavior: Throws Error('Invalid tar header. Maybe the tar is corrupted or it needs to be gunzipped?') on checksum mismatch and Error('Invalid tar header: unknown format.') when magic is neither ustar nor GNU and allowUnknownFormat is false. behavior: Parses '<len> key=value\n' records by byte length; stops on a zero/NaN length or a record without '='.

behavior: Archiver#symlink entries are not normalized: {type:'symlink', name, linkname, sourceType:'buffer', [mode], crc32:0, size:0} with no date, prefix, sourcePath or stats keys (verified).

behavior: options defaults to {} only when the argument is undefined, so create('zip-encrypted') with no options reaches the password check and throws.
hazard: null options throws a TypeError on property access instead; do not normalize null to {}.

behavior: Falsy options.password (undefined, null, '', 0) throws synchronously a plain Error with message exactly 'options.password is required'. This check runs before anything else, including the instanceof/new check.
hazard: It is a thrown plain Error, not an emitted 'error' event and not an ArchiverError with a code.

behavior: A zero-length Buffer password is truthy and is accepted (verified by running upstream); only the empty string is rejected.
hazard: Checking password.length === 0 would reject an input upstream accepts.

behavior: A non-Buffer password is converted with Buffer.from(password, 'utf-8'); the password bytes used for both ciphers are the UTF-8 encoding of the string. A Buffer password is used as is (test passes Buffer.from('123')).
hazard: No normalization (NFC), no latin1/cp437; a truthy non-string non-Buffer such as 123 makes Buffer.from throw a TypeError, which propagates.

behavior: The caller's options object is mutated: options.password is replaced by the Buffer. Zip.call also writes defaults into the same object (after construction it holds comment '', forceUTC false, namePrependSlash false, store false, zlib {level:1}, forceZip64 false, forceLocalTime false; verified by running upstream).
hazard: Copying options first changes what a caller observes on its own object afterwards.

behavior: Callable without new: ZipEncrypted(options) returns a new instance (test 'fallback construction'). Password validation and mutation happen before the re-dispatch, so they run twice harmlessly.
hazard: An ES class cannot be called without new; needs a function wrapper or Proxy to keep the test passing.

behavior: Zip.call(this, options) runs the stock Zip plugin constructor first, which builds a plain unencrypted ZipStream engine; that engine is then discarded and this.engine is replaced by the encrypting stream. Instance own keys are options, supports, engine.
hazard: The discarded engine has no observable output; a port may skip creating it but must keep the option defaulting side effects.

behavior: encryptionMethod is matched case-sensitively: 'aes256' selects ZipAesStream, 'zip20' selects ZipCryptoStream. The engine receives the same options object (password, zlib, store, comment, forceZip64, forceLocalTime, namePrependSlash, salt).
hazard: 'AES256' or 'zipcrypto' are rejected; there is no default method.

behavior: Any other value throws synchronously a plain Error: "Unsupported encryption method: '<value>'. Please use either 'aes256' or 'zip20'." with the value interpolated (missing gives 'undefined'). It is thrown after the password check, so a missing password wins when both are absent.
hazard: Order of the two checks and the literal message text.

behavior: Prototype inherits from archiver's Zip plugin: append(source, data, cb) calls this.engine.entry, finalize calls this.engine.finalize, on/pipe/unpipe forward to this.engine. No method is overridden at plugin level; all encryption lives in the engine.

All stock zip options keep their meaning for encrypted archives (comment, forceLocalTime, forceZip64, store, zlib, level, namePrependSlash), because the engines subclass ZipStream and call its constructor with the same options.
256-entry table built with the reflected polynomial 0xedb88320, 8 shift rounds per entry. Entries are JS signed int32 values (result of ^), bit-identical to the standard CRC-32 table.
hazard: Use u32 in Rust; the JS values are negative for entries with the top bit set. [PORTING.md 10.1]

behavior: One-byte update without pre or post inversion: (oldCrc >>> 8) ^ CRC_TABLE[(oldCrc ^ byte) & 0xff]. Operator precedence makes the shift bind before the xor.
hazard: Calling a normal crc32 function (which xors with 0xFFFFFFFF in and out) gives wrong keys.

behavior: Constructor accepts a Buffer or anything Buffer.from accepts (a string key is UTF-8 encoded; the test passes '123'), then runs _init immediately.

Initial keys key0=0x12345678, key1=0x23456789, key2=0x34567890; then _updateKeys is applied for every password byte in order. Golden vector from running upstream: password '123' gives key0=e0be8d5d key1=70bb3140 key2=7e983fff.
key0 = crc32(key0, b).
key1 = (key1 + (key0 & 0xFF)) mod 2^32, then key1 = (key1 * 134775813 + 1) mod 2^32. JS does this with & 0xFFFFFFFF and Math.imul.
hazard: Use wrapping_add / wrapping_mul on u32. In TS a plain * would lose precision above 2^53.

behavior: key2 = crc32(key2, key1 >>> 24), i.e. the unsigned top byte of key1.
hazard: >> instead of >>> sign-extends in JS and gives a wrong table index input.

behavior: tmp = key2 | 2; stream byte = ((tmp * (tmp ^ 1)) >>> 8) & 0xFF using a 32-bit wrapping multiply. Equal to the PKWARE 16-bit formulation.
cipher byte = streamByte XOR plain byte; keys are then updated with the plaintext byte.
hazard: Updating keys with the ciphertext byte on the encrypt side breaks everything after the first byte.

behavior: plain byte = streamByte XOR cipher byte; keys are updated with the decrypted (plaintext) byte.

Returns a new Buffer of the same length; input is not modified. Cipher state persists across calls, so chunk boundaries do not affect output. Golden vector: fresh cipher with key '123' encrypting 'hello world!' gives 28f94f360b86831bd528b11a.
hazard: Empty input returns an empty Buffer and leaves the state untouched.

behavior: Mirror of encrypt using _decryptByte; new Buffer of the same length; state persists across calls.

Transform stream, callable without new (the test does so). Takes options.key (Buffer or string) and options.crc (4-byte Buffer holding the CRC-32 big-endian, as returned by CRC32Stream.digest()). The whole options object is also handed to Transform.
hazard: crc is a big-endian Buffer here, not a number.

behavior: ZipCrypto encryption header is 12 bytes, generated as crypto.randomBytes(12) once per entry.
hazard: Upstream has no injection point for these bytes; archiver-wasm needs one for deterministic tests (10 effective random bytes). [PORTING.md V10: injectable through zip20Header / header] [PORTING.md V10: archiver-wasm draws them at the start of every entry, upstream inside the first CryptoStream._transform (ENCRYPTED-117)]

hazard: The BE read followed by LE write is easy to flip; byte 11 must be crc >> 24, byte 10 must be (crc >> 16) & 0xff.

behavior: The check bytes always come from the CRC. The DOS-time variant (used by other tools when general purpose bit 3 is set) is never used, not even when a data descriptor ends up being written (see ENCRYPTED-052).
hazard: Do not add the time-based check byte as an improvement.

behavior: All 12 header bytes are encrypted with the password-initialised cipher and pushed as one chunk; the same cipher instance continues into the file data, so data keys depend on the plaintext header bytes.
The header is emitted lazily inside the first _transform call. There is no _flush, so a stream that is ended without any write emits zero bytes: no header at all.
hazard: This is observable in archives (ENCRYPTED-050). Emitting the header at construction or in finish changes bytes.

behavior: Each data chunk is encrypted and pushed as one chunk; a zero-length result is not pushed (but the header is still emitted if this was the first call). Callback is invoked synchronously.
Transform stream (callable without new) taking options.key and options.crc; crc is stored and never used: the 12-byte header is decrypted and thrown away with no password check.
hazard: Needed only because test/crypto-stream.js requires it; a wrong key yields garbage, not an error.

behavior: Input is accumulated until more than 12 bytes have arrived (strictly greater). Then the first 12 bytes are decrypted to advance the keys and the remainder of the current chunk (data.slice(12 - header.length), a negative index) is decrypted and pushed. While at most 12 bytes are buffered nothing is output.
hazard: With exactly 12 input bytes in total the header is never processed; the strict > must be kept. The negative slice selects the last (header.length - 12) bytes of the current chunk.

behavior: Decrypted chunks of non-zero length are pushed and counted in totalSize, readable through getTotalSize().

hazard: The entry encoder must emit nothing into the archive until end of entry; streaming the compressed bytes out would require a descriptor and change bytes. Its output is piped into the archive with end:false.

hazard: _afterAppend must run before the callback; the archive may finish inside it.

behavior: A compressor or encrypt-stream 'error' is only stored; the entry is still completed and written, and the stored error is delivered as the first argument of the entry callback together with the entry.

Result: headers declare csize 12, size 0, crc 0, flags 0x1, method 0, but zero data bytes follow the local header (verified: 'd/' entry has csize=12 and 0 data bytes).

hazard: Stored stream entries get version 20 while stored buffer entries get version 10 (verified).

behavior: A source 'error' (first one only) is re-emitted on the compressor and the compressor is ended, so the truncated entry is still written in full with the CRC of what was read, and the error reaches the entry callback.
